issues.legal_issue: A release by an heir apparent of an expected inheritance, though ineffective as a transfer under Section 6(a) of the Transfer of Property Act, can create an equitable estoppel when made for valuable consideration and relied upon by the property owner.
An equitable estoppel arising from an ancestor’s conduct can bind descendants claiming inheritance through that ancestor, preventing them from asserting the inherited property right.

The prohibition in Section 8(1) of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act against a guardian binding a minor by a personal covenant does not apply where the minor had no existing right in the property when the covenant was made.
